channel.title: IPD radar — capsid & nanomaterial design
channel.description: Weekly automated literature radar for protein design, self-assembly and structural machine learning.

item.title: MYC targeted de novo binders impair tumor growth
item.description:
Designed binders target conserved intrinsically disordered epitopes on MYC itself, depleting MYC-dependent tumor cells across five cancer models where small molecules have never worked.
McNamara-Bordewick, N. K., …, Baker, D. · bioRxiv · 16 Oct · function-design · action: read

item.title: Complex enzyme active site scaffolding by iteratively detuned catalytic guidance
item.description:
Fades classifier-free guidance on RF3 over repeated design cycles so a sequence settles into satisfying several catalytic-geometry constraints at once, instead of fighting them simultaneously.
Qian, T., …, Baker, D. · bioRxiv · 16 Oct · enzyme · action: read

item.title: Generative steering to adapt proteins beyond native biological contexts
item.description:
A test-time annealing sampler converts secreted human renin into an active cytosolic protease and strips HLA-binder epitopes from antibody fragments, without retraining the generator.
Zhang, X., …, Gao, X. J. · bioRxiv · 18 Oct · design-method · action: read

item.title: Structural analysis of de novo-designed binders targeting the closed state of HSP90.
item.description:
Cryo-EM confirms BindCraft's predicted structures atom-for-atom, and the two designed binders selectively lock HSP90's closed conformation, a state no small-molecule inhibitor has ever reached.
Srivastava D, …, Artemyev NO · Structure (London, England : 1993) · 16 Oct · design-method · action: read

item.title: Rigidity-Aware Geometric Pretraining for Protein Design and Conformational Ensembles
item.description:
Pretrains on 432K AlphaFold-DB structures under simulated rigid-body perturbations before generative finetuning, front-loading geometric understanding instead of learning it incidentally from design labels.
Ni, Z., …, Liu, S. · bioRxiv · 18 Oct · ml-method · action: skim

item.title: De novo design of metalloenzymes using Metal Mer
item.description:
Metal Mer maps backbone geometry directly onto statistically preferred metal-coordination modes, then builds the catalytic core around the product, reaching >99% ee on 13 substrates with no directed evolution.
Shan, C., …, Lu, L. · bioRxiv · 16 Oct · enzyme · action: read

item.title: Seq2Pocket: Augmenting protein language models for spatially consistent binding site prediction.
item.description:
Smooths residue-level pLM binding-site predictions with embedding-aware post-processing so the output pocket is one contiguous patch instead of scattered false fragments.
Škrhák V, …, Hoksza D · Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) · 16 Oct · struct-pred · action: skim

item.title: GOLD: Geometric Optimized Latent Diffusion for Structure-Aware RNA Inverse Folding
item.description:
Projects discrete RNA sequence and continuous side-chain angles into one shared latent manifold, so backbone and sequence co-diffuse instead of being generated in separate, incompatible spaces.
Qi Si, …, Yuan Cheng · arXiv · 16 Oct · ml-method · action: skim

item.title: Relation-Aware Graph-Hypergraph Networks for Antibody Sequence-Structure Co-Design
item.description:
Models the antibody-antigen interface as a hypergraph instead of pairwise edges, so cooperative multi-residue effects in CDR design finally have an architecture built for them.
Wei, J., …, GUO, J. · bioRxiv · 18 Oct · function-design · action: read

item.title: LigRNA: High-accuracy prediction of RNA-ligand binding sites via dynamic chemical complementarity and language model encoding
item.description:
Encodes ligands as attributed molecular graphs rather than fixed fingerprints, then cross-attends them against structure-aware RNA embeddings to predict exact binding residues instead of just binding or not.
Wang, X., …, Xiong, P. · bioRxiv · 17 Oct · struct-pred · action: skim

item.title: Kinetic-driven microphase separation and vitrification of crowded hydrogels with associative bonds.
item.description:
A crowded associative-bond hydrogel resolves into either homogeneous vitrification or confined microphase separation depending purely on the competing timescales of elastic relaxation versus diffusive demixing along the approach trajectory, not on which state is the free-energy minimum.
BLINDSPOT · Shi D, …, Gong JP · Science advances · 16 Oct · ml-method · action: track

item.title: Good to know: Ig Nobel Literature Prize, 1996
item.description:
Eagerly publishing research that they could not understand, that the author said was meaningless, and which claimed that reality does not exist.
GOOD TO KNOW · Ig Nobel · 1996 · Ig Nobel Prizes · Annals of Improbable Research

item.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
item.description:
Trains an all-atom generator on 1.8M structures paired with 50M+ residue-aligned captions, so you can write what you want a protein to look like or do and get a structure conditioned directly on that text, like text-to-image but for backbones.
Joseph Lee, …, Pang Wei Koh · arXiv · 9 Oct · design-method · action: read

item.title: De novo protein design in an expanded chemical space
item.description:
Loosens the pair-representation conditioning in a pretrained all-atom structure model while keeping chemical anchors fixed, so noncanonical residues and PTMs become native building blocks the generator can place and denoise around, not post-hoc substitutions.
Li, Y., …, Liu, T. · bioRxiv · 9 Oct · design-method · action: read

item.title: Design of Orthogonal Far-Red, Orange and Green Fluorophore-binding Proteins for Multiplex Imaging
item.description:
Splits a de novo dye-binding protein into two halves that only reconstitute fluorescence when both halves are present at the same subcellular location, turning a designed binder into a proximity sensor, and separately gives the binder a covalent nucleophilic-aromatic-substitution active site to lock onto its dye.
Tran, L., …, Baker, D. · bioRxiv · 9 Oct · function-design · action: read

item.title: Filling the Missing Puzzle: Integrating Interaction and Evolutionary Information to Enhance Protein Fitness Prediction in Inverse Folding
item.description:
Builds inverse folding around a heterogeneous residue-ligand graph fused with ESM-2 embeddings, so sequence design gets scored on whether it preserves the actual physical contacts to a bound ligand rather than backbone geometry and evolutionary likelihood alone.
Wang, Z., …, Li, W. · bioRxiv · 11 Oct · struct-pred · action: read

item.title: Chain of Structures: Connecting Reasoning and Generation for Protein Design
item.description:
Alternates a language-reasoning model and a structure-generation model round by round, catalytic core then active site then global backbone then full sequence, so each reasoning step directly conditions the next generation step and the resulting geometry feeds back into the next reasoning decision.
Cai, Q., …, Zhang, Z. · bioRxiv · 11 Oct · enzyme · action: read

item.title: kitAb: an automated framework for assay-specific antibody developability modeling and large-scale landscape analysis
item.description:
Instead of one fixed developability score, fits a separate regression per assay from 59 interpretable descriptors, because which physicochemical property actually predicts an assay's readout turns out to depend entirely on which assay you're predicting.
Trofimova, E., …, Ramensky, V. · bioRxiv · 11 Oct · function-design · action: skim

item.title: AutoHMD: Scalable and Accurate Validation of Antibody-Antigen Complexes by Heated Molecular Dynamics.
item.description:
Reheats antibody-antigen docking poses and watches which ones hold their interface together under thermal stress, since near-native complexes stay stable while wrong poses fall apart, succeeding where static scoring functions can't tell the two apart.
Souza JS, …, Silva JHM · Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) · 9 Oct · struct-pred · action: skim

item.title: The CAHRA Challenge: A Community-Wide Assessment of Cryo-EM Heterogeneous Reconstruction Algorithms
item.description:
Builds three separate benchmark datasets that each isolate one normally-entangled failure mode of cryo-EM heterogeneity analysis, compositional mixtures, continuous conformational flexibility, and pose-conformation confound, so algorithms can finally be scored against ground truth on each one independently.
Feathers, J. R., …, Zhong, E. · bioRxiv · 10 Oct · wetlab-method · action: skim

item.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
item.description:
Instead of generating a reasoning-plus-tool-call trajectory left to right, denoises the whole interleaved trajectory at once, so each tool-use decision is made with the full context of what comes before and after it rather than only what came before.
Mengdi Liu, …, Shiguang Shan · arXiv · 9 Oct · ml-method · action: track

item.title: De Novo Design of Flavoproteins with Controlled Excited State Dynamics
item.description:
Folds QM/MM MD and time-dependent DFT excited-state calculations directly into the design loop, not just post-hoc characterization, so the same thermostable scaffold with and without a heme-binding site lets them dial flavin redox and excited-state behavior while X-ray confirms near-angstrom design accuracy.
Anderson, R., …, Mulholland, A. J. · bioRxiv · 10 Oct · enzyme · action: read

item.title: How Fluctuations Control Chiral Symmetry Breaking in Reacting Mixtures of Chiral Molecules
item.description:
This models chiral symmetry breaking in small reacting populations as a stochastic, fluctuation-driven selection problem rather than a thermodynamic one, deriving how finite-population noise decides which of several equivalent states a system commits to and how long that commitment takes.
BLINDSPOT · Leonardo Silva-Dias, Christoph A. Weber · arXiv · 9 Oct · ml-method · action: track

item.title: Good to know: Aspartate Transcarbamoylase
item.description:
Key biosynthetic enzymes are regulated by their ultimate products through allosteric motions.
GOOD TO KNOW · Molecule of the Month #215 · RCSB PDB-101 · illustration by David S. Goodsell

item.title: Multimodal reasoning for broadly neutralizing antibody discovery from label-free human B cell repertoires across virus families
item.description:
Closes the loop between multimodal reasoning and wet-lab screening to mine natural B-cell repertoires directly, turning a ~55% neutralization hit rate into broadly neutralizing antibodies without any synthetic library design.
Hantao Lou, …, Xuetao Cao · arXiv · 2 Oct · function-design · action: read

item.title: IDRF: Inverse-Distilled Reward Fine-tuning of Masked Discrete Diffusion Models
item.description:
Fine-tunes a discrete diffusion model's few-step sampler with policy-gradient RL by bounding the usual intractable sequence-level KL penalty through inverse distillation, and shows it works on DNA sequences as well as text and images.
Vladislav Gromadskii, …, Alexander Korotin · arXiv · 2 Oct · ml-method · action: read

item.title: Serum IgM crosslinks hepatitis B subviral particles into supramolecular immune complexes
item.description:
Catches serum IgM in the act of stitching hepatitis B subviral particles into supramolecular complexes, resolving three distinct Fc-core crosslinking architectures at 2.8 angstroms directly from patient serum.
Liu, C., …, Ke, Z. · bioRxiv · 2 Oct · assembly · action: skim

item.title: Multiobjective VHH discovery through integrated high-throughput screening and AlphaFold3-guided structural prioritization.
item.description:
Uses AlphaFold3 complex predictions as a structural filter to pull the rare polyspecific VHHs that bind a conserved epitope across multiple snake toxins out of a sea of promiscuous yeast-display hits.
Overath MD, …, Jenkins TP · Science advances · 30 Sep · function-design · action: skim

item.title: EnsPlex: Integrative Protein Complex Prediction through Multi-source Complementary Structural Sampling and Topology-Aware Candidate Selection
item.description:
Treats complex prediction as a candidate-selection problem, pooling AF-Multimer, AF3, Boltz-1 and expanded docking, then learns a DockQ-trained reranker to pick the single best model instead of trusting any one generator.
Hu, B., …, He, X. · bioRxiv · 2 Oct · struct-pred · action: skim

item.title: Equivariant Flow Matching for Electron Density Prediction
item.description:
Replaces pointwise regression of electron density with SE(3)-equivariant flow matching over the full orbital-coefficient space, so the model learns a probability path instead of a single best guess.
Chenxing Liang, …, Shuiwang Ji · arXiv · 2 Oct · ml-method · action: track

item.title: Topology-enforced synthesis of atomically precise silver nanoclusters in 3D DNA lattices.
item.description:
Encodes silver-cluster nucleation directly into DNA triangle topology inside a 3D lattice, so crystal geometry rather than solution chemistry fixes cluster size and intercluster spacing to atomic precision.
Perren L, …, Vecchioni S · Science advances · 2 Oct · assembly · action: track

item.title: Auditing Protein-Protein Interaction Signals with Sparse Autoencoder Fingerprints
item.description:
Turns a protein-language-model PPI predictor's embeddings into sparse, auditable fingerprints and finds most of its apparent accuracy is a partner-independent shortcut that evaporates under topology-controlled splits.
Zhu, W., …, Pan, X. · bioRxiv · 2 Oct · struct-pred · action: cite · touches: oracles predicting whether a designed subunit assembles, without experimental positives

item.title: Distinct allosteric remodeling of HIV-1 Env dynamics on virions by gp41-directed antibodies reveals two modes of neutralization.
item.description:
smFRET shows gp41 bNAbs allosterically lock Env prefusion conformation
Xu W, …, Lu M · eLife · 2 Oct · immunogen

item.title: Once yearly cell-based therapy for sustained and dose-tunable delivery of monoclonal antibodies.
item.description:
encapsulated-cell alginate implant gives year-long sustained mAb delivery
Fell C, …, Veiseh O · Science advances · 2 Oct · delivery

item.title: Surface Charge--Potential Relation for Spherical Particles in Electrolyte Solutions
item.description:
Derives closed-form surface charge-potential relations for charged spheres across the full curvature range, replacing numerical Poisson-Boltzmann solving with an exact dual-asymptotic formula that spans weakly curved to highly curved regimes.
BLINDSPOT · Olga I. Vinogradova, Elena F. Silkina · arXiv · 2 Oct · struct-pred · action: track

item.title: Good to know: Ig Nobel Economics Prize, 2005
item.description:
Inventing an alarm clock that runs away and hides, repeatedly, thus ensuring that people DO get out of bed, and thus theoretically adding many productive hours to the workday.
GOOD TO KNOW · Ig Nobel · 2005 · Ig Nobel Prizes · Annals of Improbable Research

item.title: Drug-controlled CAR T cells through the regulation of cell-cell interactions.
item.description:
Library-optimized human protein-protein interaction parts, not a degron, give CAR T cells a venetoclax-gated off-switch that dials down tumor killing by releasing the targeting scFv rather than shutting the cell down.
Scheller L, …, Irving M · Nature chemical biology · 19 Feb · function-design · action: skim

item.title: State-selective inhibition of alpha-synuclein aggregation by de novo oligomer-binding proteins
item.description:
De novo binders trained against a beta-strand conformation of disordered alpha-synuclein don't just block fibril growth generically — one of them prefers oligomers over monomer and hits the intermediate most tied to toxicity.
Zhang, Y., …, Knowles, T. P. J. · bioRxiv · 25 Sep · function-design · action: read

item.title: FoldMark: Safeguarding Protein Structure Generative Models with Distributional and Evolutionary Watermarking
item.description:
A watermark trained into RFdiffusion, AlphaFold3, ESMFold and RFdiffusionAA survives downstream structural-quality filtering and traces a design back to one of a million users, at a cost most designers wouldn't notice in scTM score.
ZHANG, Z., …, Wang, M. · bioRxiv · 26 Sep · design-method · action: track

item.title: Targeted finetuning enables co-folding models to learn ligand-induced protein conformational states
item.description:
Ten unseen X-ray structures of one helicase are enough to finetune Boltz-1 into recognizing an allosteric site and the conformational change it locks in, and that logic transfers to other RecQ-family helicases the model never saw.
Gorantla, R., …, Sesterhenn, F. · bioRxiv · 27 Sep · struct-pred · action: read

item.title: SurfGraphPro: Integrating Protein Language Models with Geometric Deep Learning On Coarse Protein Surfaces for Binding Site Prediction
item.description:
Swapping hand-crafted surface features for protein language model embeddings on a coarse triangulated mesh gets binding-site prediction 18-28x faster without losing accuracy, and skips the MSA step entirely.
Habib, A., …, Hu, B. · bioRxiv · 25 Sep · struct-pred · action: read

item.title: AnewDDE: An Agentic Drug Discovery Engine for Biomolecular Interaction Modelling and Closed-Loop Design
item.description:
One pipeline chains a co-folding model, an affinity estimator and a binder generator into a closed loop and gets single-digit-nanomolar nanobodies in 10.7% of attempts, which is really a claim about how much SPR bench time the loop saves.
Anew Labs Team,, Liu, K. · bioRxiv · 25 Sep · design-method · action: skim

item.title: Computational design of a thermostable α-helical barrel protein with tunable active-site positioning
item.description:
A six-helix antiparallel barrel with a non-natural fold gives enzyme designers a thermostable scaffold whose central channel lets you slide the catalytic site to different positions without redesigning the whole protein.
Elaily, W., …, Oberdorfer, G. · bioRxiv · 25 Sep · enzyme · action: read

item.title: In-cell discovery and characterization of a non-canonical bacterial protein translocation-folding complex.
item.description:
In-cell cryo-electron tomography of a genome-reduced bacterium catches the Sec-translocon mid-secretion, and the mystery dome bolted onto its surface turns out to be three foldase-like proteins homologous to the periplasmic chaperone PrsA rather than anything previously described.
Jensen RK, …, Mahamid J · Cell · 25 Sep · wetlab-method · action: read

item.title: Control of ice thickness in cryo-EM via confinement.
item.description:
Graphene reservoirs pin the liquid film before plunge-freezing so it stops self-thinning at an arbitrary point, turning cryo-EM ice thickness from a fight against instability into a dial you set by reservoir depth.
Zheng L, …, Wang HW · Nature methods · 25 Sep · wetlab-method · action: read

item.title: Discovery of noncanonical cytochrome P450 enzymes in nature.
item.description:
Two decades after the proximal cysteine was called obligatory for every cytochrome P450, a genome search turns up serine- and selenocysteine-ligated variants, the latter never seen in any P450 before.
Nguy AKL, …, Seyedsayamdost MR · Nature chemical biology · 22 Jun · enzyme · action: skim

item.title: A Bonded-Particle Discrete-Element Model with Self-Gravity for the Collision and Reaccumulation of Rubble-Pile Asteroids: Formulation and Numerical Protocol
item.description:
A bonded-particle discrete-element model of rubble-pile asteroids sweeps collision speed and impact parameter to map exactly where two self-gravitating bodies merge into one versus fail to reaccumulate, with merger governed by competition between short-range bond-breaking dissipation and long-range mutual gravity.
BLINDSPOT · Yohann Trivino · arXiv · 25 Sep · ml-method · action: track

item.title: Good to know: Insulin Receptor
item.description:
The cellular receptor for insulin helps control the utilization of glucose by cells
GOOD TO KNOW · Molecule of the Month #182 · RCSB PDB-101 · illustration by David S. Goodsell

item.title: De novo design of cysteine proteases
item.description:
An activated-cysteine nucleophile hydrolyzes the peptide backbone itself, not just an ester — 13 of 69 designs worked, on folds with no natural precedent (TM < 0.50) and crystal structures within 1.2 A of the model.
Choi, H., …, Baker, D. · bioRxiv · 21 Sep · enzyme · action: read

item.title: Computational design of metalloproteases
item.description:
RFdiffusion2's interface mode builds zinc proteases from minimal catalytic motifs instead of grafting whole active sites, and the best hit cleaves 10^10-fold faster than the uncatalyzed reaction after four preorganization mutations.
Chen, A., …, Baker, D. · bioRxiv · 21 Sep · enzyme · action: read

item.title: Latent generative search unlocks de novo design of untapped biomolecular interactions at scale
item.description:
Reward-guided search steers a codesigned sequence-and-structure latent model at inference time instead of redesigning sequences post-hoc, and wins a phage screen of over a million designs against every other binder method, including on polar epitopes that resist hydrophobic contacts.
Didi, K., …, Kreis, K. · bioRxiv · 18 Sep · design-method · action: read

item.title: Charged residues, not aromatics, are the universal topological hubs of intrinsically disordered proteins
item.description:
Arginine and lysine carry identical net charge but only arginine acts as a network hub in IDP contact maps — hub character comes from charge-carrier geometry, not charge itself, and every taxon shows the same positionally-encoded pattern.
Rahman, T., Uversky, V. N. · bioRxiv · 18 Sep · assembly · action: read

item.title: Virtual experiments bridge sequence and microscopy with generative models
item.description:
Trains a generative model to translate protein sequence into fluorescence microscopy images and back, so virtual mutagenesis of an IDR reads out condensate formation without running a single real experiment.
Zheng, D., …, Huang, B. · bioRxiv · 18 Sep · ml-method · action: read

item.title: Linear antibody epitope prediction using AlphaFold2.
item.description:
Breaks the antigen into overlapping linear peptides and folds each against the antibody chains with AlphaFold2, flagging known epitopes without ever running a binding assay.
DeRoo J, …, Geiss BJ · eLife · 18 Sep · struct-pred · action: skim

item.title: VirPLM: Antigenic prediction of influenza A/H3N2 viruses with a fine-tuned protein language model.
item.description:
Fine-tunes ESM-2 on HA1 sequences to predict antigenic distance directly, replacing the labor-intensive hemagglutination-inhibition assay, and holds up under retrospective time-split evaluation.
Li X, …, Kong H · Bioinformatics (Oxford, England) · 18 Sep · immunogen · action: skim

item.title: A Unified 3D Generative Model for Synthesizable Structure-Based Drug Design
item.description:
One generative model handles docking, fragment linking/growing, and de novo design together, then a programmable algorithm constrains output to synthesizable routes, validated against five real targets.
Igashov, I., …, Correia, B. · bioRxiv · 18 Sep · ml-method · action: skim

item.title: EM3DFold: accurate de novo protein and nucleic acid model building for cryo-EM maps using language model-powered deep learning
item.description:
A density-aware three-track network builds all-atom models straight from cryo-EM maps, hitting 94% sequence accuracy on nucleic acids where manual building has always been the bottleneck.
Li, T., …, Huang, S.-Y. · bioRxiv · 18 Sep · wetlab-method · action: skim

item.title: Optimizing the connectivity of protein conformations to untangle ensemble refinement
item.description:
Formulates picking low-energy conformer combinations as an integer-linear program instead of gradient refinement, and escapes the 'tangled' trap that strands every current ensemble-refinement method on a synthetic benchmark.
Passmore, S. K., …, Martin, A. V. · bioRxiv · 19 Sep · struct-pred · action: read · touches: quasi-equivalence: one sequence, multiple backbone conformations by assembly slot

item.title: Repulsive normalizing flow mixtures for adaptive importance sampling: reliability analysis of complex systems
item.description:
FAMIS learns a repulsion-regularized mixture of normalizing-flow proposals that discovers multiple rare-event failure modes adaptively, with no presampled failures and no prior knowledge of how many modes exist or where they lie.
BLINDSPOT · Sara Helal, Victor Elvira · arXiv · 18 Sep · ml-method · action: track

item.title: Good to know: Ig Nobel Physics Prize, 1999
item.description:
Calculating the optimal way to dunk a biscuit, and Jean-Marc Vanden-Broeck of the [UK and Belgium], and Joseph Keller [USA] for calculating how to make a teapot spout that does not drip.
GOOD TO KNOW · Ig Nobel · 1999 · Ig Nobel Prizes · Annals of Improbable Research
